architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Using the directly measured 120-130 C viscosity-level change relative to the unmodified reactive-core reference, accept exactly one registered level hypothesis only if the measured change is within 3.4 percentage points of its prediction: -42.76% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 17.24% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or -72.76% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. Report the directly measured 120 and 130 C levels and the candidate-specific E_eta with the accepted formulation-level hypothesis.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The primary viscosity-level observable does not depend on transferring a rheological regularity from another chemistry family: it is measured directly in the selected resin_modified:ac1920+tk100 chemistry at 80-130 C. The candidate-specific E_eta is therefore supported over the measured temperature range, while the prior unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI shared shape must not be assumed transferable. This is a formulation-level rheological result, not a molecular-mechanism test.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the measured 120-130 C level change differs from -42.76% by more than 3.4 percentage points. H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if the measured change is at or below -42.76%. H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if the measured change is at or above -42.76%. If preparation-to-preparation variation exceeds 3.4 percentage points, the result is not treated as reliable separation of the level hypotheses; it instead falsifies the claimed single-preparation discrimination resolution.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run S1C41::M-REPEAT to quantify between-preparation spread using at least three independently prepared samples and 80-130 C sweeps before accepting or rejecting a level hypothesis at the 3.4% resolution.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level at 120 and 130 C, with viscosity measured across 80-130 C in 10 C increments and the apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from regression of ln(eta) versus 1/T.
judge_normalized.rationale: M-SWEEP directly measures the processing-window level in the selected chemistry and simultaneously establishes its temperature response, avoiding unsupported shared-shape transfer. It is therefore the most scientifically defensible probe for separating inert dilution, acrylic-like elevation, and plasticizing depression at the formulation level. The dual-axis formulation and large observed realization variability prevent molecular attribution and may leave the registered hypotheses unresolved despite the direct sweep.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator in selecting direct S1C41::M-SWEEP rather than the deterministic tied M-ANCHOR cards. The chemistry audit is advisory, but it identifies M-ANCHOR as inadmissible before shape verification because the shared shape is unvalidated for resin_modified:ac1920+tk100. I followed the Skeptic by treating the 3.4% criterion as conditional on quantified preparation-state variation, not as reliably attainable from the nominal one-preparation protocol.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: The three registered level hypotheses are directly tested for this dual-axis composition, but AC1920 and TK100 contributions remain confounded. The experiment cannot attribute the result separately to either modifier axis.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Low for the viscosity level within 80-130 C because the level is directly measured there; high if the prior unmodified-family thermal shape is transferred or if E_eta is interpreted outside the measured range.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The M-SWEEP discrimination threshold is 3.4% multiplicative RMSE, but this is a fit residual rather than a demonstrated total uncertainty for this modified candidate. Instrumental and regression uncertainty affect the measured levels and E_eta.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: High. The supplied local evidence reports comparable sweep CV values of 0.464-0.585 and max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57. Controlled preparation history and independent preparation repeats are required before interpreting a 3.4% difference as decisive.

action_requests.reason: The audited upstream material structure and chemistry-supported local rheology must be loaded before candidate or experiment ranking and before deciding whether a shared thermal-response shape can be transferred.

action_requests.reason: Retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, E2 reactive-core anchor, modifier axes, and historical boundary needed to compare candidate experiments without using the blinded follow-up formulation.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local rheological regularities were measured in the original E-series reactive polyurethane hot-melt reactive-core family, including the original same-composition comparisons and the separately verified E1 +P chemical perturbation. The intended experiment would stay inside that family only if it uses a registered acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like lattice modification without introducing a chemistry-changing modifier such as AC1920 or TK100; because the prospective candidate identity is not supplied, applicability must be audited before using a shared-shape shortcut.
planner.failure_mode: The modified candidate may fall outside the processing-viscosity window because the realized viscosity level is strongly dependent on temperature and preparation state.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: For E2, measured viscosity decreased from a mean of 18530.6667 at 80 C to 3322.0 at 130 C, while nominal repeat spread was large across the sweep (sample CV 0.464-0.585 and max/min ratio 2.80-3.57).
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local data provide temperature-response sweeps for E1-E3 and isothermal trajectories for E1 and E5, but no direct level measurement exists for the prospective candidate. The E2 level is also poorly reproducible, with CV values of 0.464-0.585 and max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57 across 80-130 C; viscosity units and the processing-window limits remain unspecified.
measurement_requirements: Directly measure the candidate's viscosity level over 80-130 C in 10 C increments on a freshly prepared sample rather than reconstructing the processing-window level from a single anchor.
Record the realized level at 120 and 130 C and compare it with the inert-dilution, acrylic-association, and plasticization predictions at matched temperature.
Use a controlled and fully recorded preparation history and report repeat measurements or preparation spread so chemistry effects can be distinguished from realization-state uncertainty.
Report the candidate's measured temperature-response descriptor and restrict interpretation to the measured temperature range.
planner.scientific_question: At matched temperature and controlled preparation state, does the candidate's realized viscosity level follow inert dilution, rise above dilution as predicted by acrylic association, or fall below dilution as predicted by plasticization, and is the shared thermal-response shape valid for transferring the level across the processing range?

planner_action_requests_after_forcing.reason: The audited upstream material structure and chemistry-supported local rheology must be loaded before candidate or experiment ranking and before deciding whether a shared thermal-response shape can be transferred.

planner_action_requests_after_forcing.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
planner_action_requests_after_forcing.reason: Retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, E2 reactive-core anchor, modifier axes, and historical boundary needed to compare candidate experiments without using the blinded follow-up formulation.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: The primary processing-window level is measured directly by the temperature sweep rather than reconstructed from the shared thermal-response shape. Therefore the observable does not depend on transferring the unmodified-family regularity into the resin-modified AC1920/TK100 chemistry. The sweep also directly tests whether that thermal-response shape is valid for this candidate. The 15% acrylic-like and 5% minor-tackifier-like loadings lie within the externally supported intervention regions.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If the directly measured 120-130 C level change falls within the 3.4% M-SWEEP resolution of exactly one registered prediction, that hypothesis is accepted for this composition and the directly measured processing-window level is reported with it. The sweep additionally establishes the candidate-specific thermal-response shape over the measured range.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If the result is at or below the inert-dilution prediction, H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified; if it is at or above the inert-dilution prediction, H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified; if it departs from the inert-dilution prediction by more than 3.4%, H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified. Such an outcome would reject the corresponding level explanation while retaining the direct level and shape measurements.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result not resolvable within 3.4% of one prediction would leave the registered level hypotheses unresolved at this candidate and indicate that measurement or realization-state uncertainty exceeds the discrimination threshold. The directly measured thermal response would still determine whether shared-shape transfer is locally defensible.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level across 80-130 C, including the realized viscosity level at 120 and 130 C, together with the apparent temperature-response descriptor E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Although its deterministic VOI is highest, it reconstructs the 120-130 C level from a single 110 C anchor using a shared shape that was measured only in the unmodified chemistry family. The audit marks this card inadmissible before shape verification, so its apparent discrimination is conditional on an unverified chemistry transfer.

It directly measures thermal-hold drift and is highly interpretable, but it does not return the processing-window level needed for the stated failure mode and cannot separate the three registered level hypotheses.
It addresses preparation-state spread rather than the candidate's processing-window level and cannot separate the registered dilution, association, and plasticization level predictions.

proposer.reasoning: The audit is advisory, but the local shared-shape regularity has not been verified for S1C41's resin-modified AC1920/TK100 chemistry. M-SWEEP therefore provides the most scientifically defensible direct test of the decision quantity, separates all three registered level hypotheses at the stated resolution, and simultaneously verifies the candidate-specific thermal response without relying on an extrapolated model fit.

robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: The proposal S1C41::M-SWEEP departs from the deterministic tied top set, which contains five S1C41/S1C46/S1C51/S1C56/S1C61 M-ANCHOR cards. The departure is scientifically justified because M-ANCHOR relies on an unverified shared-shape transfer into resin-modified AC1920/TK100 chemistry, whereas M-SWEEP measures the processing-window level directly and verifies the candidate-specific thermal response.
residual_decision_risk: Preparation-state variability may exceed the declared hypothesis-discrimination threshold.
The registered level hypotheses may remain unresolved after direct measurement.
The dual-axis intervention confounds acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like effects.
The apparent E_eta descriptor remains regression-dependent and is not a molecular or kinetic mechanism.
The prior unmodified-family shared thermal-response shape must not be transferred to this chemistry without candidate-specific verification.
The deterministic stability report describes score stability, not model confidence, posterior probability, or correctness.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection does not favor a different measurement card: it supports retaining direct M-SWEEP but shows that the stated 3.4% discrimination criterion is not attainable with one preparation. The experiment should therefore use multiple independent preparations with fully recorded process history and repeated sweeps, estimate candidate-specific preparation spread, and treat the three level hypotheses as unresolved unless the enlarged uncertainty supports separation. The dual-axis design also cannot attribute an outcome separately to AC1920 versus TK100, and the fitted E_eta descriptor should not be interpreted mechanistically.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: No tested weight perturbation changes the tied deterministic top set: top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, all recommendation_flip_boundary entries survive the entire 0.5-1.5 sweep, and no flipped scenarios were observed. The base margin to the first strictly lower experiment is 0.002292. These perturbations are defensible sensitivity checks, but they do not establish scientific validity; the tied top set remains dominated by M-ANCHOR cards whose chemistry-domain applicability is unvalidated. The proposal remains preferable on chemistry-support and direct-observation grounds, not because of VOI stability.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary viscosity level stays inside the measured support of the proposed experiment because S1C41::M-SWEEP directly measures the resin-modified AC1920/TK100 candidate from 80 to 130 C. It does not stay inside the prior unmodified-family shared-shape support; that shape is unvalidated for this chemistry and must not be reused. Candidate-specific direct sweeps and adequate repeatability are required before any later one-point anchor transfer could be justified.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The criterion is mathematically specified but not practically attainable with the stated protocol. The 3.4% threshold is a fit residual, not a demonstrated total uncertainty for a single fresh preparation. The observed local state variability is orders of magnitude larger than 3.4%, and M-SWEEP has min_repeats set to 1 with no required preparation-spread estimate. A result therefore cannot reliably meet the criterion as a hypothesis falsification rather than as an uncontrolled realization difference.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result could support or reject an aggregate level hypothesis, but would not support the claim that AC1920 association, TK100 plasticization, or their individual contributions caused the observed level.
objections.objection: For S1C41, the registered level predictions are numerically separated: approximately -42.76% for H-LEVEL-DILUTE, 17.24% for H-LEVEL-ASSOC, and -72.76% for H-LEVEL-PLASTIC, versus the M-SWEEP discrimination threshold of 3.4%. However, the experiment cannot distinguish an acrylic-specific effect from a minor-tackifier-specific effect because both axes are changed simultaneously at 15% AC1920 and 5% TK100. It separates the three aggregate registered level predictions, not the causal contribution of either modifier axis.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Mechanism attribution to acrylic association versus tackifier plasticization, and any claim about which axis is responsible for the result, becomes unsupported.
objections.objection: The proposed formulation changes both modifier axes at once: AC1920 is 15.0 wt% and TK100 is 5.0 wt%, while the reactive core is reduced to a reactive mass fraction of 0.80. The dual-axis intervention therefore confounds acrylic-like loading, minor-tackifier-like loading, and the associated replacement of reactive material. The experiment has no single-axis comparator in the proposed protocol.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The direct viscosity-level conclusion remains usable, but any stronger conclusion based on E_eta as an independent mechanistic descriptor would be overstated.
objections.objection: The processing-window viscosity level at 120 and 130 C is directly measured by M-SWEEP across 80-130 C, so the primary level observable does not require the shared-shape extrapolation used by M-ANCHOR. However, the accompanying E_eta descriptor is obtained by regressing ln(eta) against 1/T and therefore inherits the regression model and residual assumptions; it is not a directly observed molecular or kinetic quantity.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Using the prior shared shape to interpret S1C41 would reintroduce the inadmissible M-ANCHOR assumption and could make the processing-window level unsupported.
objections.objection: The proposed M-SWEEP does not reuse the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI shared thermal-response shape to reconstruct the candidate level. S1C41 is explicitly classified as resin_modified:ac1920+tk100 with modified_chemistry_unvalidated status, and the audit recommends M-SWEEP with shared_shape_use set to verification_only. Because the sweep directly measures 80-130 C behavior in this candidate chemistry, the primary level observable stays within the measured support of the proposed experiment. The candidate-specific curve must nevertheless be used for interpretation; the prior unmodified-family shape cannot be treated as transferred evidence.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A failure to match a registered prediction could reflect preparation-state variation rather than falsification, while an apparent match could be accidental; the claimed discrimination among level hypotheses would not be practically defensible.
objections.objection: The M-SWEEP falsification threshold is declared as 3.4%, based on a multiplicative RMSE from a shared-shape plus intercept-only fit. But S1C41::M-SWEEP specifies only one freshly prepared sample, while the supplied local evidence reports E2 sweep CV values of 0.464-0.585 and max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57 across 80-130 C. The protocol also does not require the controlled, fully recorded preparation history or repeated independent preparations requested by the planner. Thus the 3.4% criterion is much smaller than the demonstrated realization-state variability and cannot reliably be met by the specified measurement.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A level match could be incorrectly reported as proof of molecular association, plasticization, or functionality-dependent chemistry rather than as evidence for a formulation-level rheological pattern.
objections.objection: The proposal does not appear to use post-result formulation or outcome information; its candidate and rationale are supported by the pre-result payload. However, the rheological sweep can establish the realized level and candidate-specific thermal response only. It cannot establish a molecular association mechanism, a plasticizing molecular mechanism, or the H2 functionality claim. The registry explicitly limits the level hypotheses to formulation-level statements and states that none asserts a molecular association mechanism.

skeptic.recommended_change: Retain the direct S1C41::M-SWEEP rather than M-ANCHOR, but require multiple independent preparations with fully recorded process history and repeated 80-130 C sweeps. Estimate the candidate-specific preparation spread before applying any 3.4% discrimination rule, and either enlarge the acceptance resolution to include that uncertainty or declare the level hypotheses unresolved. If axis attribution is required, add separately measured single-axis candidates rather than interpreting the dual-axis result mechanistically.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The declared 3.4% M-SWEEP discrimination and falsification resolution is not attainable as specified: the protocol uses only one preparation, does not control or quantify preparation-state variation, and the local evidence shows 46.4-58.5% CV and 2.80-3.57-fold spread for comparable viscosity sweeps. Consequently, the experiment cannot reliably distinguish the three predictions at the claimed resolution.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_GJJ_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 GJJ day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is ADVISORY. Every experiment card above remains selectable, including the cards the audit marks inadmissible. Use the audit as scientific evidence and justify whatever you select.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.
